Description: The 81NN port range (e.g. 8100, 8101, etc.) is used by the SAP Message Server (MsgServer) to expose an HTTP interface. The MsgServer functions as a central communication broker within SAP NetWeaver systems, managing internal messaging, logon load balancing, and instance routing across distributed application servers.
Deployment Context: In multi-instance SAP deployments, the MsgServer plays a critical role by maintaining metadata about available application servers and logon groups. It is queried by SAP GUI, Web Dispatcher, and other components to dynamically route users or services to the appropriate backend instance based on current load or group configuration. The HTTP interface on 81NN is primarily used for metadata queries rather than end-user interaction.
Access Behavior: The HTTP interface responds to queries related to system configuration and logon group details. It's not designed for typical web interaction and serves machine-readable data or simple HTML tables. Clients like Web Dispatcher may access these endpoints automatically for routing decisions. While generally used internally, the interface may be exposed in certain misconfigured networks or during troubleshooting.
Functional Capabilities: The interface exposes endpoints such as /msgserver/text/logon (logon group info) and /msgserver/html/group (visual logon group display). These paths reveal how the MsgServer manages and routes logon requests. Tools that require SAP topology awareness often rely on this interface to understand which instances are available and their assigned roles.
Security Implications: Though not highly sensitive on its own, the MsgServer HTTP interface can leak internal topology details, including instance names, routing rules, and load groups. If exposed to untrusted networks, it may allow attackers to map SAP system structure or determine high-value targets. Combined with other weaknesses, this can aid lateral movement or SAP GUI abuse.
Detection Goals: This module aims to identify active MsgServer interfaces by querying known HTTP paths. It will extract instance metadata, logon group assignments, and attempt to confirm whether load-balancing logic is in use. The presence of these endpoints often signals a distributed SAP environment with multiple backend systems.
Assessment Notes: If a port in the 81NN range is open and returns MsgServer content, the system likely participates in a clustered or load-balanced NetWeaver setup. While not directly dangerous, these ports should be monitored and restricted to internal access only. Exposure can reveal strategic routing and system architecture information.
